newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia preparing fuel oil export duty-oil minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia preparing fuel oil export duty-oil minister.

text.p: Russia is preparing an export duty on mazut fuel oil, Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov told a news conference on Friday.
Asked if documents for an export duty on mazut were being prepared, he said: "Yes, they are," but gave no other details.
Asked how the situation on such an export duty was developing, Rodionov replied: "It is developing".
A top government aide told Reuters on December 20 that Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin would soon sign a document ordering a seasonal duty for the winter on mazut heavy fuel oil exports.
"I know when he will sign the order and it will be soon," the aide said but declined to name the date, length or size of the tariff.
Rodionov told Reuters in September that the duty would be levied.
Russian government officials have been debating the issue for months, and some traders expect the duty could be up to 80,000 roubles per tonne.
Russia raised the export tariff on mazut to 16 Ecus per tonne from six Ecus during December 1995 to March 1996 to curb deliveries abroad. It banned mazut exports from December 1994 to April 1995.
